stem: An alcoholic patient presents with palpitations, dizziness and syncopal attacks. On examination the pulse is irregularly irregular. What will be seen on the JVP?
concept: An irregularly irregular pulse in a chronic alcoholic points to atrial fibrillation ('holiday heart'). Because the atria fibrillate rather than contract in a coordinated way, the atrial-systole 'a' wave of the JVP disappears. A large a wave is seen in tricuspid stenosis/pulmonary hypertension, a cannon a wave in AV dissociation (complete heart block/VT), and a steep y descent in constrictive pericarditis.
subject: Physiology
topic: Cardiac cycle, ECG basis, BP regulation
